data.title: Anthropic's stock slides closer to IPO price and drags down the AI trade
data.description:
By Emily Bary

Anthropic's inability to hold its opening stock price has been seen as 'bad for the rest of tech'

Anthropic finished with a $1.29 trillion valuation on Thursday.

There was no honeymoon period for Anthropic after its record-breaking initial public offering.

Shares of the AI company are down more than 9% in morning action on Friday, making for a gloomy second day of trading. Anthropic's stock (ANT) is at $88.16, well below its $111.50 opening price, and falling closer to its $83 IPO price.

It's a downbeat sign for the broader technology ecosystem as well, with AI stocks taking a beating across the board. Among notable losers are shares of Sandisk (SNDK), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Dell Technologies (DELL), Nebius Group (NBIS) and Arm Holdings (ARM).

"The vast majority of this continued selling pressure in the last 24 hours feels more to do with" the Anthropic IPO than it does with some less-than-perfect earnings reports in the technology sector, according to Jefferies trading-desk analyst Jeffrey Favuzza.

He wrote in a note to clients that Anthropic's inability to hold its opening price and the downward pressure in Friday's premarket action is being viewed as "bad for the rest of tech."

Anthropic's IPO was seen as a tentpole event for the AI trade. The company finished with a $1.29 trillion valuation on Thursday, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Friday's action brings that down to $1.16 trillion.

"Anthropic's strong debut alongside a falling technology sector suggests investors still believe in AI but are becoming more selective about what they will pay for that growth," David Miller, the chief investment officer at Catalyst Funds, said in emailed comments.

Some analysts initiated coverage of Anthropic's stock after Thursday's close, chiming in with mixed views.

Don't miss: After Anthropic's 'bittersweet' IPO, here's what lies ahead

"We are cautious, not negative," wrote Seaport Research's Jay Goldberg, who launched coverage of shares with a neutral rating.

He called Anthropic an "incredible company," but also one "asking for an incredible leap of faith by investors."

"We think the company will need time to grow into its valuation and answer some very big questions about its growth trajectory," he continued. For instance, the company saw 43% revenue growth from the second quarter to the third quarter. That compared with a much faster 144% growth rate from the first quarter to the second quarter.

Goldberg referred to that as a "worrying" deceleration. "To merit its valuation, it will need to see much higher growth rates over the next two years," he added.

William Blair's Arjun Bhatia was more upbeat, calling Anthropic a "generational company driving a generational technology shift" as he began his own coverage of the stock with an outperform rating.

"Questions about the future are worth asking, even those that don't have an answer at this point," he wrote.

But at the same time, he and his team "don't want to miss the forest for the trees."

"We think AI is a generational shift in the tech landscape, and Anthropic is leading the charge in developing AI with a select handful of other companies," Bhatia wrote. "Over the next decade, we think Anthropic is only going to become more important and consume a greater portion of enterprise spend," meaning it will command more of the budget that businesses have to allocate toward technology.

See also: Anthropic soared in its debut as stocks tanked. Only one other IPO has done that since 1990.

-Emily Bary

What Does Homeowners Insurance Cover? Insurance Expert Kathy Thurmond-Edwards Clarifies Water Damage Risks

PR Newswire

MEMPHIS, Tenn., Nov. 20, 2026

Kathy Thurmond-Edwards explains how burst pipes, flooding, gradual leaks, and sewer backups can affect homeowners insurance coverage.

KEY HIGHLIGHTS

  • Homeowners insurance may cover sudden and accidental water damage from burst pipes, depending on the cause and policy terms.
  • Flood damage from rising outside water generally requires separate flood insurance, while gradual leaks are often excluded.
  • Optional water backup coverage may protect against certain sewer backups and drain overflows that standard policies exclude.

MEMPHIS, Tenn., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Does homeowners insurance cover water damage from a burst pipe, leaking appliance, or flooded basement? Kathy Thurmond-Edwards, an insurance expert in Memphis, Tennessee, clarifies how different causes of water damage affect coverage in a HelloNation article. Her insights help homeowners understand common exclusions and identify potential coverage gaps before damage occurs.

data.title: ICE Canada Morning Comment: ICE Canola Futures Softer
data.description:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba--ICE canola futures were posting small losses Friday morning as values continued to chop around in narrow, rangebound trade.

The January contract was down $2.50 at C$774.50 per tonne in early activity.

Overnight losses in Chicago soyoil, European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil accounted for some spillover selling pressure.

Canada exported 141,000 tonnes of canola during the week ended Nov. 15, which was roughly half of what moved the previous week, reported the Canadian Grain Commission.

However, marketing-year-to-date exports of 2.66 million tonnes remain well ahead of the 1.83 million tonnes exported by the same point in 2025-26.

Updated supply/demand estimates from Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada included only minor adjustments to the canola balance sheet, with projected 2026-27 ending stocks lowered to 1.87 million tonnes from 1.97 million in October.

Projected exports for the year were left unchanged at 7.7 million tonnes, while domestic usage was raised by 100,000 tonnes to 14.5 million.

About 14,300 canola contracts had traded as of 8:46 a.m. ET.

data.title: I'm terrified of a market crash. Should I put $400,000 of my $1 million retirement savings into an annuity?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'We have a house worth $450,000. Our combined annual income is $125,000.'

"We don't have any nonqualified brokerage investments, and our combined annual income is $125,000." (Photo subjects are models.)

Dear Quentin,

I'm wondering what your thoughts are on putting our house and other assets into a trust. Could it help reduce taxes or protect our assets from lawsuits, bankruptcy or other unforeseen circumstances? If so, what are the potential downsides or pitfalls?

We have a house worth $450,000 and about $1 million in retirement assets held in various qualified accounts. I'd also be interested in your thoughts on annuities for capital preservation and guaranteed income.

Would it make sense to put $400,000 of our $1 million in qualified retirement accounts into an annuity that would begin paying out at age 65, guaranteeing us $40,000 a year for life, while leaving the remaining $600,000 invested in a brokerage account for capital appreciation?

My spouse and I are 55 and 54, respectively. We're both working and plan to continue until 65. We're terrified of a market crash. We don't have any nonqualified brokerage investments, and our combined annual income is $125,000.

Curious in the Midwest

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: 'Nvidia has me spooked ': Should I sell my stocks or buy real estate?

That money you invest in an annuity is no longer readily available, and you give up any stock-market gains it might have earned.

Dear Curious,

I'll outline the advantages of your proposal - and then move on to the cons.

First, the pros of putting your money in an annuity, I presume, are to find a haven for part of your nest egg, albeit at a potentially lower rate than the stock market could provide. If you moved $400,000 from traditional 401(k)s or IRAs into an IRA annuity, the transaction generally would not trigger income taxes or the 10% early-withdrawal penalty, provided the funds are transferred correctly. A direct trustee-to-trustee transfer is typically the simplest approach. If you were selling $400,000 worth of investments in an ordinary brokerage account, however, you could owe capital-gains taxes on any profits realized from the sale.

Annuities provide guaranteed income, much like Social Security, which you presumably plan to take when you reach full retirement age. What you receive depends on the type of annuity: your initial investment, the interest rate or other terms you lock in and, of course, the payment schedule. Payouts can also vary with your age, your sex and whether the product is a joint-life annuity. If you expect to live a long time, a lifetime annuity can protect you from outliving your retirement savings. The trade-off is access: That money is no longer readily available, and you give up any stock-market gains it might have earned.

Annuities provide guaranteed income, much like Social Security.

An annuity is neither a bond nor cash. It works as an insurance contract: you pay an insurance company in exchange for income. An immediate annuity starts paying within a year of purchase, while a deferred annuity starts at a later date. Money in a 401(k) or IRA that is invested in stocks can grow over time and help keep pace with inflation. Annuity income is usually fixed, so it can lose purchasing power as prices rise unless you add an inflation adjustment or rider, but that protection also comes at a price: a lower initial payout. Annuity fees can be as much as 10% of the value of your contract. Surrender charges can be substantial if you withdraw money early.

But I have some questions: I understand why the prospect of $40,000 in guaranteed annual income is tempting. If payments continued for those periods, you would collect $400,000 over 10 years, $800,000 over 20 years and potentially $1.2 million over 30 years. Make sure you read the fine print. Is that $40,000 guaranteed income for one person's lifetime? Or is it for both of your lifetimes? Does the surviving spouse continue to receive the full $40,000-a-year income? Is there a death benefit or return-of-premium provision or rider if one spouse dies? Last but not least, are the $40,000-a-year payments adjusted for inflation?

Don't miss: My wife and I are in our 70s. Should we pay off our 2.5% mortgage or invest in a stock market driven by AI?

Investing in the stock market

Third, the pros of leaving the money in the stock market: If you left your $400,000 invested for another 10 years instead of putting it into an annuity, it could grow to approximately $592,000 at an annual return of 4%, $787,000 at 7%, or $864,000 at 8%. These estimates assume annual compounding, with investment earnings reinvested, and exclude taxes, fees and additional contributions. The biggest difference between this scenario and the option of buying an annuity with your $400,000 is that the former is not guaranteed. You are potentially giving up the prospect of a larger return in exchange for security.

An annuity and a trust provide different estate-planning functions. Annuities distribute your assets per the terms of the contract, whereas a trust is designed to manage, protect and distribute your estate during your lifetime and beyond. As this guide on Estate Guru points out, trusts and annuities solve different estate-planning problems: (1) Bypassing probate or buying an annuity isn't an estate plan. (2) A trust can manage your assets if you become incapacitated, provide for minor children or beneficiaries with special needs, address the complications of a blended family and set out the conditions for an inheritance.

Revocable living trusts can benefit people with modest estates, particularly those seeking to avoid probate or plan for incapacity. For families with complicated estates, putting accounts and assets under a single trustee can keep everything running smoothly. It can also help prevent conflicts involving beneficiary designations. Marital trusts matter most in blended families, where each spouse wants to be sure their own children are provided for if the other dies. A special-needs trust can supplement government benefits, while a spendthrift trust can prevent beneficiaries from selling or using their future inheritance as collateral for a loan.

Know what you're buying, and be sure you're doing it for the right reasons.

Related: Is Social Security a Ponzi scheme? No. Don't get carried away with 1930s-era prophecies of doom.

data.title: GameStop has transformed from a meme stock into a 'real company,' analysts say
data.description:
By Bill Peters

Roaring Kitty's return had minimal impact on GameStop's stock, which has started to gain more sophisticated appeal for its 'new and improved story'

GameStop shares are up 34% so far this year.

After Roaring Kitty's reawakening on Thursday nudged GameStop's shares only modestly higher, some analysts are declaring the meme trade dead for the videogame and collectibles retailer.

The chain (GME), after being cast off by many analysts, no longer needs to rely simply on meme-stock energy for gains, according to Mike Hickey, an analyst at StoneX. Rather, shares stand to benefit from the ongoing collectibles boom and the launch of "Grand Theft Auto VI," as gamers download the game and upgrade their equipment to play it.

"It's a real company, and it's trading at what we think is a very undervalued price," Hickey said of GameStop.

When his firm previously covered GameStop, it had a sell rating and a price target of zero, he said. When the chain was swept up in the meme-stock frenzy, they stopped covering it, he noted: "But that trade is over."

Few analysts cover GameStop. But StoneX this month initiated coverage of GameStop shares with a buy rating and a $33 price target. Analysts there noted that the company, which over the years had closed hundreds of stores, stood to gain from select reopenings announced in September.

"September's announcement of selective U.S. store reopenings adds a new growth catalyst, while expanded collectibles space and dedicated fixtures could improve productivity within existing locations," the note said.

Dan Ives, senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., echoed the optimism.

CEO Ryan Cohen "is turning GameStop into a collectibles story with massive efficiency," he said over email. "This is no longer a meme stock; it's in the process of becoming a new and improved story."

He added: "GameStop will still have many retail fans but we see it as a very undervalued asset."

On Thursday, a new post showing a picture of Cat Mario, appeared on the X account for Keith Gill, the investor known as Roaring Kitty, whose enthusiasm for GameStop created a retail-trading stampede into the stock in 2021. At the time, that ruined short sellers' bets against the company. But unlike previous spikes that followed arcane posts in years past, shares of GameStop only rose around 1.5% on Thursday.

Over the stock's roller-coaster journey since 2021, analysts have cast doubt on GameStop. They have cited losses, uneven sales, disruption from e-commerce and a shift toward online gaming. There are also general concerns about the videogame industry's ability to sustain demand as consumers struggle with higher prices for essentials. Some analysts have predicted that the chain might not survive the 2020s. And Wall Street questioned GameStop's efforts to buy or otherwise collaborate with eBay (EBAY).

In the second quarter, GameStop's sales fell 18.7% to $790.2 million. But revenue from collectibles - things like trading cards and action figures - jumped 57% and made up 45.1% of sales.

GameStop in September also raised its forecast for adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization - a profitability metric - to more than $650 million for its full fiscal year, which ends on Jan. 30.

The collectibles market has taken off thanks to nostalgia and the card industry's focus on rarities and limited drops. Quarterly sales of "Magic: The Gathering" have risen past $600 million, Hasbro (HAS), which makes the game, said last month. Shares of collectible figurine maker Funko (FNKO) have roughly doubled this year.

Shares of GameStop are up 34% over that period, and trading at around $27. That's still well off their 2021 highs. But Hickey still believes in the stock.

"There's really no other stock that you can buy that gives you that much exposure to collectibles, which we think is a durable opportunity," Hickey said.

"When we're out there talking to people, the first thing that people ask is, 'Are you serious? Isn't that a meme stock?'" he added. "We're serious as serious gets, and no, it's not a meme stock."

-Bill Peters

data.title: Tsingke Highlights How Biotech Teams Can Evaluate and Advance Antibody Candidates at PEGS Europe 2026
data.description:
Tsingke Highlights How Biotech Teams Can Evaluate and Advance Antibody Candidates at PEGS Europe 2026

Tsingke Highlights How Biotech Teams Can Evaluate and Advance Antibody Candidates at PEGS Europe 2026

PR Newswire

LISBON, Portugal, Nov. 20, 2026

From early antibody hits to engineered formats and antibody–oligonucleotide conjugates, Tsingke helps R&D teams generate the data they need to make the next development decision.

LISBON, Portugal, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- An antibody that binds its target is a starting point for drug discovery. R&D teams still need to determine which candidates can be produced for follow-up studies, which retain the desired binding properties in the intended format, and which merit further investment. At PEGS Europe 2026 in Lisbon, Tsingke highlighted how pharmaceutical and biotechnology teams can address these questions through an integrated workflow spanning antibody discovery, recombinant expression, engineering and characterization.

Which early antibody hits are worth advancing?

Teams starting with an immune sample or existing hybridoma clones may need to turn a list of hits into a set of recombinant antibodies they can compare. Tsingke's single B-cell screening workflow preserves native heavy- and light-chain pairing, while hybridoma sequencing gives teams a route to recover sequences from existing clones. Once candidates are expressed, teams can compare binding using assays selected for the project, such as cell-based binding by flow cytometry or binding kinetics measured by BLI or SPR. These data help teams prioritize candidates for follow-up testing.

Will the antibody retain the properties the program needs?

When a program moves an antibody into a different format, such as a Fab or scFv, the team needs to know whether the reformatted molecule still meets its binding criteria. Teams can use recombinant expression and binding characterization to compare formats before committing to more extensive studies. For programs that require different binding behavior at different pH values, Tsingke also supports pH-dependent screening and engineering, with characterization tailored to the program's objectives.

What does the team need to know before testing an antibody–oligonucleotide conjugate?

For teams evaluating an antibody–oligonucleotide conjugate (AOC), the next decision often depends on having a characterized sample for follow-up studies. Tsingke brings together antibody production, oligonucleotide synthesis, conjugation, purification and LC-MS characterization. The resulting analytical data help teams assess the conjugated material and select samples for subsequent functional evaluation.

"Teams come to us at different points in development. Some have early antibody hits and need a consistent way to compare them. Others already have a lead and need to understand how a change in format or conjugation affects the molecule they plan to test," said Yuan Wu, International BD Manager at Tsingke. "We start with the decision the team needs to make and align the production and characterization work with that decision."

About Tsingke

Beijing Tsingke Biotech Co., Ltd. provides molecular biology and biologics research services to pharmaceutical, biotechnology and academic teams. Its services include custom DNA and RNA synthesis, antibody discovery, recombinant protein production, antibody engineering and analytical characterization.

For company updates, follow Tsingke Biotech on LinkedIn.

data.title: Momcozy Expands into the Food Category with Its First Lactation Cookies
data.description:
Momcozy Expands into the Food Category with Its First Lactation Cookies

Momcozy Expands into the Food Category with Its First Lactation Cookies

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Nov. 20, 2026

A vegan, individually wrapped snack made with oats, dried yeast fermentate, chia seeds, and other thoughtfully selected ingredients for breastfeeding moms.

NEW YORK, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Momcozy, a global maternal and baby care brand chosen by more than 6 million moms and families across 80 countries and regions, has launched Momcozy Lactation Cookies, marking its first expansion into the food category. Designed with breastfeeding moms in mind, the vegan cookies combine traditional lactation-cookie ingredients with convenient, individually wrapped packaging, offering a practical snack option for busy days.

Understanding the Everyday Nutrition Needs of Breastfeeding Moms

Breastfeeding asks a lot of moms, from frequent nursing and pumping sessions to the many responsibilities that come with caring for a newborn. With so much of the day focused on their babies, finding time to prepare and enjoy nourishing food can easily become an afterthought. A quick snack may be easy to reach for, but moms also want options that offer nutritional value and fit their individual dietary preferences.

To better understand these needs, Momcozy analyzed 2,630 pregnancy- and maternity-related discussion posts across Reddit, YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, and Pinterest. The analysis identified three prominent themes in postpartum and breastfeeding conversations: the need for nutritional support, convenient snack options, and concerns related to lactation. These findings highlight the importance of accessible food options that fit into the demands of everyday breastfeeding life.

Momcozy Lactation Cookies were created with these needs in mind, offering a ready-to-eat snack made with familiar ingredients and designed to fit into busy breastfeeding routines. The cookies provide a convenient option for moms looking to prioritize their own nutritional needs while caring for their little ones.

Inside Momcozy's 4+2 Lactation Nutrition Blend

Momcozy Lactation Cookies feature a 4+2 Lactation Nutrition Blend that combines four ingredients commonly found in traditional lactation cookie recipes—oats, dried yeast fermentate, chia seeds, and flaxseeds—with two additional ingredients: sunflower lecithin and pumpkin seeds.

Each 20 g cookie contains 400 mg of sunflower lecithin, a plant-based ingredient valued for its phospholipid content, along with 2 g of protein. Together, these ingredients offer breastfeeding moms a convenient snack option made with familiar ingredients and designed to fit into their everyday routines.

A Snack That Considers Different Dietary Preferences

Momcozy Lactation Cookies are made with a vegan recipe that excludes soy, milk, eggs, wheat, and peanuts as ingredients, offering an option for moms with different dietary preferences. The recipe also leaves out traditional lactation herbs such as fenugreek, blessed thistle, and goat's rue, as well as artificial colors, preservatives, and flavors.

Available in cranberry chocolate caramel flavor, the cookies combine these ingredient choices with an enjoyable taste, offering breastfeeding moms a convenient snack that fits into their everyday routines.

Made to Fit the Moments That Make Up a Breastfeeding Day

Designed for the different rhythms of breastfeeding life, Momcozy Lactation Cookies are individually wrapped for easy snacking between pumping sessions, during outings with the baby, or throughout the workday. Available in 10-cookie and 20-cookie packs, they offer a convenient option that requires no preparation or portioning.

Supporting Every Part of the Breastfeeding Journey

With the introduction of Lactation Cookies, Momcozy continues expanding how it supports breastfeeding moms beyond traditional pumping equipment. From wearable breast pumps to convenient snack options, the brand is developing products designed around the everyday needs of moms throughout their breastfeeding journeys.

To celebrate the launch, Momcozy Lactation Cookies will be available at 20% off from now till November 30, 2026.

About Momcozy

Founded in 2018, Momcozy is a global maternal and baby care brand dedicated to helping moms feel comfortable, confident and supported throughout motherhood. Through thoughtful, technology-driven innovation and products designed around real needs, Momcozy supports families through pregnancy, postpartum recovery, breastfeeding and everyday parenting.

Chosen by more than 6 million moms and families across 80 countries and regions, Momcozy has ranked No. 1 globally in wearable breast pump sales volume for five consecutive years (2021–2025), according to Frost & Sullivan's 2026 research. Momcozy is available online at Momcozy.com and through major retailers including Babylist, Walmart, Target and Amazon.

data.title: FlexFactor Wins Two Honors at The Card & Payments Awards US 2026 for Industry Innovation and the Future of Payments
data.description:
FlexFactor Wins Two Honors at The Card & Payments Awards US 2026 for Industry Innovation and the Future of Payments

FlexFactor Wins Two Honors at The Card & Payments Awards US 2026 for Industry Innovation and the Future of Payments

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Nov. 20, 2026

After leading the inaugural U.S. awards as the only six-time finalist, FlexFactor earns double recognition for transforming when and how payment decline recovery happens.

NEW YORK, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- FlexFactor, the AI-powered payments technology company pioneering real-time decline decisioning during authorization, today announced it won two awards at The Card & Payments Awards US 2026, held November 17 at Gotham Hall in New York City.

FlexFactor entered the inaugural U.S. ceremony as the only six-time finalist and finished the evening tied for the most awards won by any organization. The company took home two honors, Best Industry Innovation and Best Early-Stage or Future Payments Initiative, in recognition of both the innovation FlexFactor is delivering today and its potential to shape the future of payments tomorrow.

The awards highlight FlexFactor's fundamentally different approach to payment decline recovery. Instead of building a better retry or dunning tool, FlexFactor moved recovery into the authorization moment itself, using real-time decisioning to reverse eligible false declines before legitimate customers ever see a failed payment.

FlexFactor's proprietary AI-powered intelligence platform, AcceptIQ, evaluates declines in seconds to determine the optimal path to recovery. For recoverable transactions, FlexFactor purchases the merchant's invoice, guarantees the sale, and assumes the recovery risk. The result is more completed sales for merchants and a seamless customer experience, without the disruption of a declined payment.

Already live with more than 100 merchants, FlexFactor delivers cure rates ranging from 5% to 30% of eligible false declines, typically translating into a 0.5% to 3% uplift in gross sales. Results vary by merchant profile, decline mix, and payment environment. Beyond recovering otherwise lost revenue, FlexFactor helps merchants protect customer lifetime value, maximize the return on customer acquisition investments, and preserve the customer experience.

"At FlexFactor, we're obsessed with solving one problem: reversing false payment declines," said Philip McHugh, CEO of FlexFactor. "Our approach reduces negative customer moments and experiences while giving ecommerce merchants greater flexibility and certainty to drive incremental sales. These awards recognize the impact of solving a longstanding payments problem in a fundamentally different way."

"Being the only six-time finalist was a statement. Bringing home two awards makes an even bigger one," said Brennen Creer, CMO of FlexFactor. "Every transaction we recover is more than a sale saved. It's a customer who never knew they were almost turned away, and a merchant who keeps a relationship they worked hard to earn. We're excited to keep pushing the boundaries of what's possible alongside our partners and the merchants they serve."

The 2026 ceremony marked the inaugural U.S. edition of The Card & Payments Awards, an internationally established awards program recognizing excellence and innovation in the payments industry since 2005. Winners were selected through an independent judging process involving industry experts.

The two wins add to FlexFactor's growing list of 12+ industry honors, including the 2024 ETA Award for Most Innovative Product or Solution and the 2024 VIP Award for Best Payment Innovation.

About FlexFactor

FlexFactor is redefining payment decline recovery through AI-powered real-time decline decisioning during authorization. Powered by its proprietary AcceptIQ intelligence platform, FlexFactor identifies, evaluates, and reverses eligible false declines before legitimate customers experience a failed payment. For recoverable transactions, FlexFactor purchases the merchant's invoice, guarantees the sale, and assumes the recovery risk, turning otherwise lost transactions into completed sales while protecting the customer experience. Live with more than 100 merchants and backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, FlexFactor is on a mission to ensure every legitimate customer gets the yes they deserve. Learn more at flexfactor.io.

data.title: Tokyo Lifestyle Co., Ltd. to Open New Reiwatakiya Store at Westfield London, Strengthening Its Retail Presence in the UK
data.description:
Tokyo, Japan, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Tokyo Lifestyle Co., Ltd. (“Tokyo Lifestyle” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: TKLF), a retailer and wholesaler of Japanese beauty and health products, sundry products, luxury products, electronic products, collectible cards, trendy toys as well as other products in Hong Kong, Japan, North America, Thailand, Vietnam, the United Kingdom and Australia, today announced the planned opening of a new store under its proprietary “Reiwatakiya” brand (the “Store”) in London, the United Kingdom, on November 21, 2026. This expansion marks another important milestone in the Company’s ongoing efforts to strengthen its UK retail presence, broaden its customer reach, and enhance its international sales network.

A Prime Retail Location in an Iconic Shopping Destination

Located at Westfield London, one of the largest shopping centers in the UK and Europe, the new Reiwatakiya Store is expected to benefit from substantial shopper traffic and a diverse international customer base. Supported by convenient transportation links, including underground, rail, and road networks, Westfield London and its surrounding area attract approximately 27.9 million visitors annually. The shopping center generates approximately £1 billion in annual retail sales, underscoring its position as a leading commercial and retail destination in London.

The Store will showcase Tokyo Lifestyle’s diverse selection of authentic Japanese beauty and lifestyle products, selected Korean beauty brands. Strategically situated next to Zara and Apple stores, the Store is positioned to attract a broad consumer audience, particularly younger shoppers who represent an important target demographic for the Company.

To celebrate its grand opening on November 21 and 22, the Store will host special promotional activities, including a limited-time Japanese beauty goodie bag giveaway. These initiatives are designed to attract initial customer traffic, build brand awareness and foster engagement with local consumers. For more details about the grand opening event, please visit https://reiwatakiya.co.uk/.

The new Store will complement Tokyo Lifestyle’s existing London location in the city center, strengthening its retail presence in distinct commercial areas across the city. Together, these locations are expected to enhance the Company’s brand visibility, broaden its access to local consumers and international visitors, and provide a stronger operating foundation for potential expansion into other European markets.

Advancing Global Expansion Through a Distinctive Retail Brand Strategy

The Company’s UK expansion forms part of its broader global growth strategy, guided by its commitment to bringing authentic Japanese beauty and lifestyle products, distinctive cultural experiences, and emerging consumer trends to customers worldwide. In recent years, Tokyo Lifestyle has accelerated the expansion of its international retail operations, with its latest physical store opening in Sydney in October 2026.

Alongside its expanding international retail footprint, the Company continues to pursue greater revenue diversification and brand development through a combination of directly operated stores, franchise partnerships, and wholesale distribution channels. These initiatives are intended to strengthen its international market presence, broaden its customer base, and establish a more diversified and scalable global business platform.

Mr. Mei Kanayama, Principal Executive Officer of Tokyo Lifestyle, commented: “The opening of our new Reiwatakiya store in the UK represents an important milestone in our long-term commitment to the UK and broader European markets. London has long served as a strategic gateway for our European expansion, and establishing two retail locations in distinct commercial areas across the city will enable us to reach a wider customer base, strengthen our brand recognition, and further develop our local operating capabilities.

“We have made a meaningful long-term commitment to this location, reflecting our confidence in the commercial potential of Westfield London and the continued appeal of Japanese beauty and lifestyle products among international consumers. Beyond adding another retail location, we see this Store as an opportunity to further refine our retail positioning, deepen customer engagement, and strengthen our understanding of local consumer preferences. Looking ahead, we intend to leverage our growing presence in London as a foundation for exploring additional opportunities across the UK and Europe, while continuing to build a distinctive and internationally recognized retail brand. We believe our expanding global retail network, combined with our diversified product portfolio and multi-channel business model, will position Tokyo Lifestyle to capture emerging market opportunities and generate sustainable long-term value for our shareholders.”

About Tokyo Lifestyle Co., Ltd.

Headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, Tokyo Lifestyle Co., Ltd. (formerly known as Yoshitsu Co., Ltd) is a retailer and wholesaler of Japanese beauty and health products, sundry products, luxury products, electronic products, collectible cards, trendy toys, and other products in Hong Kong, Japan, North America, Thailand, Vietnam, the United Kingdom and Australia. The Company offers various beauty products (including cosmetics, skincare, fragrance, and body care products), health products (including over-the-counter drugs, nutritional supplements, and medical supplies and devices), sundry products (including home goods), collectible cards and trendy toys (including Pokémon cards, BE@RBRICK and other trendy products) and other products (including food and alcoholic beverages). The Company currently sells its products through directly-operated physical stores, through online stores, and to franchise stores and wholesale customers. data.title: EU Open to 'Closest Possible Relationship' With U.K., Chief Says
data.description:
By Edith Hancock

The European Union is open to having a much closer relationship with the U.K., the head of the European Council said, as both sides continue work to thaw ties more than a decade after Britain voted to leave the bloc.

"We remain open to [having] the closest possible relationship between the European Union and the United Kingdom," European Council President Antonio Costa said Friday in Brussels.

U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham was in the Belgian capital for a U.K.-EU summit to sign agreements on issues including youth mobility and food exports.
